archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-first)
archetype.definition: A Metropolitan middle-of-the-pack club whose elite goaltending and penalty kill keep the goals against near the top of the league, while a low-volume attack and a thin blueline cap how far that can carry it.

report.headline: Sorokin and the penalty kill again hold up a team that rarely scores.
report.take:
Eleven games in, the Islanders look like a team they have been before. They are 5-4-2 and fifth in the Metropolitan, 14th on the site. They are fifth in goals against per game and 20th in goals for. That is the shape of 2025-26, when they ranked fifth in defense and 26th in offense, and of 2022-23, which also had a top-five defense. The formula is goaltending first, a strong penalty kill, and enough scoring to stay in games.

The goaltending carries the most weight. The goalies are third in the league in Goalies GSAx at 8.9, against a league average under one. Ilya Sorokin has a .919 save % and 5.7 GSAx over eight starts and sits sixth on the goalie tab. The team's .914 save % is fourth, while its shooting % of .112 sits almost exactly at the league's. So the PDO of 102.2 is not a shooting bubble. The lift comes entirely from the crease. That is still a source that can fade, but this franchise has posted GSAx above 40 in two of the last four seasons, so it has more staying power here than it would elsewhere. The penalty kill at 86.1% (4th) adds to it. The power play at 18.2% (22nd) is a weakness, and history says it has been one for years.

The even-strength numbers are ordinary. xGF % is 49.6 and CF % is 51, roughly break-even. The team takes only 26 shots a game, 25th in the league. The forward group grades B- and leans heavily on Bo Horvat, who has 12 points and five of them on the power play. The blueline grades D+ and is essentially Matthew Schaefer, who plays 26.21 minutes a night and ranks 14th of 250 defensemen. Behind him, Adam Pelech and Ryan Pulock sit near the bottom of the defense tab, and Pulock's xGF % is .417. The defense has been very good against opposing forwards, fourth in holding them under their expected points. Opposing defensemen, though, are producing above expectation, 24th in the league. That points to a structure that collapses well around the net but gives up the point.

The record is, if anything, slightly worse than the play. Pts vs Goal Diff is -1.3, 27th, because both overtime games were one-goal losses. The 82-game pace of 89 points sits right beside last season's 91. This looks like a 90-point team that will be in the wild-card fight all year, unless the goaltending runs even hotter than it already is.

strengths.title: Elite goaltending, again
strengths.body: Sorokin is sixth on the goalie tab with 5.7 GSAx. Even Varlamov is saving goals above expected despite an .899 save %, which says the shots he faces are dangerous ones. Team GSAx ranks third, and history backs it up: 40.1 last season. Some regression from a .914 team save % is likely, but this is the most bankable piece of the roster.

strengths.title: A top-five penalty kill
strengths.body: At 86.1% the kill is fourth in the league and far above the league average of 78.3%. It pairs with the goaltending to keep the goals against fifth-best. Some of that number is the goalie behind it, so expect it to settle a bit while staying above average.

strengths.title: Forwards smothered in front
strengths.body: Opposing forwards are scoring well under their own averages against this team, fourth-best in the league. That fits a team that keeps shots against near the league average and lets its goalie handle the rest.

concerns.title: Not enough shots, weak power play
concerns.body: Only 26 shots on goal a game, 25th, and a power play at 18.2%, 22nd, give the offense a low ceiling. Shooting at a league-average rate cannot make up for that volume. The offense has ranked 22nd or worse in each of the last five seasons, so this is structural, not a slump.

concerns.title: A blueline of Schaefer and little else
concerns.body: Schaefer's 26-plus minutes and 10 points carry a defense graded D+. Pelech and Pulock both rank below 180th on the defense tab. Opposing defensemen are out-producing their averages, 24th in the league. If Schaefer misses time, the gap behind him becomes the team's biggest problem.

concerns.title: Margin slipping lately
concerns.body: The last five games ran a goal differential per game well below the season mean. The stretch ended with a 6-3 loss in Dallas. The points have kept coming through overtime, but the underlying margin has thinned.

trend.note: They have alternated wins and losses all month, and their longest streak either way is two games. The last five took a slightly better share of points than the season average but with a thinner goal margin.

weekAhead.headline: Two road games, then Edmonton's hot shooting meets Sorokin.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens in Nashville against a team the Islanders should handle at even strength. The Predators' xGF % of 45.1 is 26th, but their power play is third, so the Islanders' fourth-ranked kill will be tested. Minnesota is the hard one. The Wild are third on the site, allow 21.7 shots a game (2nd) and own a .918 team save %. Against an Islanders attack that already struggles to generate volume, expect a low-scoring game decided by the goalies.

Edmonton at home on Halloween is the most interesting game. The Oilers are 8-2-1 with the league's best offense, but it runs on a 17.3% shooting rate, first by a distance. Their goalies are last in GSAx and their PDO is second. They lead the league in Pts vs Goal Diff. Their PK of 70% (26th) is the best chance all season for the Islanders' power play to get going.

keyMatchups.title: Islanders PP against Edmonton's kill
keyMatchups.body: A 22nd-ranked power play meets a 26th-ranked penalty kill. If the Islanders can't score with the extra man here, they will struggle to anywhere. Horvat's five power-play points make him the focal point.

keyMatchups.title: Generating shots in Minnesota
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders' 26 shots a game run into a Wild defense that allows the second-fewest. Minnesota's goalies also rank sixth in GSAx. A game in the low twenties for shots is likely, and the Islanders will need Sorokin to match.

keyMatchups.title: Nashville's power play vs NYI kill
keyMatchups.body: The Predators are outplayed at 5-on-5, but their 33.3% power play is third in the league. Staying out of the box, or killing at their usual rate, should make Nashville a game the Islanders can win.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Edmonton's league-best 17.3% shooting can beat a goalie saving goals at Sorokin's rate, or whether it finally cools against him.

restOfSeason.body:
The Islanders' pace of 89 points mirrors last season, and the profile behind it is the same: a top-five defense, a bottom-third offense and goaltending well above average. The goaltending edge should shrink some from a .914 save %, but Sorokin's track record suggests it stays a real plus rather than collapsing. The slightly negative Pts vs Goal Diff should even out, so the record and the goal differential should line up more closely. Projected finish: 85-95 standings points.

What keeps this from being more than a bubble team is the even-strength play. Their shot share is roughly even, their shot volume is low, and the defense depends on one player. Unless the power play climbs toward league average, they will stay in the wild-card race, where a Sorokin hot streak or a Schaefer absence could swing it either way.

confidence.note: Eleven games is a small sample, but the profile matches the last several seasons.
